_comment: Large world-map binaries used to be tracked in Git LFS, whose free bandwidth (1 GB/mo, shared org-wide) was exhausted by a handful of installs. They now live as assets on a GitHub Release, whose download bandwidth is free and unmetered. scripts/fetch-map-assets.mjs reads this manifest and downloads any listed file that is missing or out of date; the launcher and updater call it instead of touching Git LFS. When a map file changes: upload the new asset to the release below and update its sha256 + bytes here. The two big pmtiles are the z8 trims (scripts/trim-pmtiles.mjs): the map mounts both sources at maxzoom 8 and never asks for z9 or z10. The website fetches its own list (scripts/map-assets.web.json). A packaged beta shares the stable app's copy of these files, so change them on every branch in the same release, or the two apps re-download each other's map on every launch. The last entry is the stock GADM world that every scenario without a map of its own renders on; the built-in Modern Day scenario's OWN map is not listed here at all — it ships inside the app under server/seed/default/ and the server seeds it into the data directory (see docs/assets-and-data.md). The last two entries are one world, the editor's default world and the stock world built from it (scripts/build-default-map.mjs), and both are its deep-cleaned edition (-clean): the Scenario Workshop's save-time border cleanup at 1.5 km run to the end over the z8 extract, so a save of that map has nothing left to repair. Change the two together. The stock entry's earlierBytes lists the sizes of the editions before it, by which an install that still keeps one of them as its built-in scenario's map is recognised (server/libraryStore.js).
